chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from Ziyād ibn Abī al-Ḥalāl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no Prophet and no successor who remains in the earth for more than three days until he is raised, with his soul, his bones, and his flesh, to the heaven. Rather, people come to the places of their traces, and convey salām to them from afar, and make them hear it from nearby in the places of their traces.

key_terms.السَّلَامَ: the greeting of peace conveyed to them
key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the heaven, to which they are raised
key_terms.مَوَاضِعُ آثَارِهِمْ: the places associated with their traces or physical marks
key_terms.وَصِيٍّ: a designated successor to a Prophet or Imam

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the state of the Prophets and Awsiya' after death and the meaning of visiting their traces?
ai.summary: This hadith states that no Prophet or wasi remains in the earth beyond three days; rather, he is raised with his soul and body to the heaven. It also explains that visitation is directed to the places of their traces, where salām reaches them from afar and is heard from nearby.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3161 - Ali ibn al-Hakam narrated from Ziyad ibn Abi al-Hilal, from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"No prophet or successor remains on earth for more than three days before their soul, bones, and flesh are raised to the heavens. However, people visit the places associated with their traces, and salutations reach them from afar and are conveyed to them. From near, they hear the salutations in the places associated with their traces."
